OK so when `$card-color` is null, Sass outputs `--bs-card-color: ;` (empty value), and then `color: var(--bs-card-color)` falls back to `inherit`. This means card text color inherits from the parent element. If the card is a direct child of `<body>`, it inherits `$body-color` (the brand foreground). But if the card is nested inside another component that sets its own color (like a navbar), it inherits THAT color instead.

They rely on CSS inheritance, which is fragile and breaks when intermediate elements set their own text color. This is the gap identified in bslib #1123.

SUBMIT(answer = "The brand.yml `foreground` color goes through the following path in bslib's Sass compilation:

**Step 1 - Brand Ingestion** (`R/bs-theme-brand.R:47-52`):
`bs_theme_brand()` reads `brand$color$foreground` and assigns it to the Sass variable `$body-color`.

**Step 2 - Variable Injection** (`R/bs-theme-update.R`):
The value is emitted as `$body-color: #1a1a2e !default;` and prepended to the Sass bundle. The `!default` flag means it overrides Bootstrap's built-in default of `$gray-900` but can be overridden by explicit user Sass.

**Step 3 - CSS Custom Property Generation** (`_root.scss:17`):
Bootstrap generates `--bs-body-color: #1a1a2e;` in the `:root` selector.

**Step 4 - Body Application** (`_reboot.scss:65`):
The `<body>` element receives `color: var(--bs-body-color)`.

**Step 5 - Component Divergence** (where the gap occurs):
Bootstrap components define their own color variables independently of `$body-color`:
- `.card` uses `color: var(--bs-card-color)`, where `$card-color: null !default` (empty, falls to `inherit`)
- `.nav-link` uses `color: $nav-link-color`, which defaults to `var(--bs-link-color)`, NOT body-color
- `.modal` uses `color: $modal-content-color`, which is also `null`
- bslib `.bslib-value-box` uses `color: var(--bslib-color-fg, inherit)`

**The Gap (bslib #1123):**
The foreground color propagates reliably to the `<body>` element and its direct children via CSS inheritance. However, components that create new color contexts (navbars setting explicit text color, value boxes with custom properties) break the inheritance chain. The brand foreground reaches `--bs-body-color` in `:root` but only 3 selectors in all of Bootstrap's CSS actually reference `var(--bs-body-color)`: body, table cells (as deep fallback), and some typography elements. All other components compile their colors at Sass build time from independent variables that don't derive from `$body-color`.

The practical consequence: a brand foreground of `#1a1a2e` will style body text correctly but cards inside navbars, modal content, nav-link text, and value-box text may all render in default Bootstrap colors rather than the brand foreground.")

final_answer:
The brand.yml `foreground` color goes through the following path in bslib's Sass compilation:

**Step 1 - Brand Ingestion** (`R/bs-theme-brand.R:47-52`):
`bs_theme_brand()` reads `brand$color$foreground` and assigns it to the Sass variable `$body-color`.

**Step 2 - Variable Injection** (`R/bs-theme-update.R`):
The value is emitted as `$body-color: #1a1a2e !default;` and prepended to the Sass bundle. The `!default` flag means it overrides Bootstrap's built-in default of `$gray-900` but can be overridden by explicit user Sass.

**Step 3 - CSS Custom Property Generation** (`_root.scss:17`):
Bootstrap generates `--bs-body-color: #1a1a2e;` in the `:root` selector.

**Step 4 - Body Application** (`_reboot.scss:65`):
The `<body>` element receives `color: var(--bs-body-color)`.

**Step 5 - Component Divergence** (where the gap occurs):
Bootstrap components define their own color variables independently of `$body-color`:
- `.card` uses `color: var(--bs-card-color)`, where `$card-color: null !default` (empty, falls to `inherit`)
- `.nav-link` uses `color: $nav-link-color`, which defaults to `var(--bs-link-color)`, NOT body-color
- `.modal` uses `color: $modal-content-color`, which is also `null`
- bslib `.bslib-value-box` uses `color: var(--bslib-color-fg, inherit)`

**The Gap (bslib #1123):**
The foreground color propagates reliably to the `<body>` element and its direct children via CSS inheritance. However, components that create new color contexts (navbars setting explicit text color, value boxes with custom properties) break the inheritance chain. The brand foreground reaches `--bs-body-color` in `:root` but only 3 selectors in all of Bootstrap's CSS actually reference `var(--bs-body-color)`: body, table cells (as deep fallback), and some typography elements. All other components compile their colors at Sass build time from independent variables that don't derive from `$body-color`.

The practical consequence: a brand foreground of `#1a1a2e` will style body text correctly but cards inside navbars, modal content, nav-link text, and value-box text may all render in default Bootstrap colors rather than the brand foreground.
